# Ribbon Application Tab Scope

## How To Build

A RibbonApplicationTabScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A RibbonApplicationTabScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

The ribbon's Application tab: the commands for the application itself, rather than the project.

### Shape

#### Description

The Application tab of the ribbon, last of the tabs.

#### Groups

```
appearance: An "Appearance" group holds the Brightness command, its one control; there is no Dark mode switch, since the slider reaches both modes.
colours: A "Colours" group, between Appearance and Preferences, holds the Theme command.
preferences: A "Preferences" group holds the Settings command.
help: A "Help" group, the last, after Preferences, holds the Welcome command, then the Walkthrough command, then the Check for Updates command.
```

#### Commands

```
brightness: A "Brightness" slider, which runs the whole interface from its darkest to its lightest: a moon icon, then a horizontal slider 120 pixels wide, then a sun icon, with nothing showing the setting as a number. As a ribbon setting, it has no background of its own, and sits straight on the commands' area, as tall as a slim button. Its tooltip says it makes the whole interface darker or lighter, from its darkest to its lightest, keeping its contrast, and that double-clicking it resets it.
  Its one track runs through every appearance the [ThemeScope](../../../theme/index.md#theme-scope) allows, darkest first: dark mode from its darkest brightness to its lightest, then light mode from its darkest to its lightest, one position for each step, with no switch between them. So all the way left is dark mode at its darkest, and all the way right light mode at its lightest; dragging past dark mode's lightest step changes the window to light mode, and back.
  Dragging it changes the mode and the brightness straight away as it moves, and once it is let go saves the mode showing and each mode's brightness among the [UserPreferencesScope](../../../../scope/user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope). A mode that can't be saved shows a notification titled "Could not save brightness", with why; a brightness that can't be saved fails quietly. Its thumb follows the appearance showing, however that was changed, such as from the palette, but not while it is being dragged.
  Double-clicking anywhere on it, its icons or its track, puts the mode showing back to its brightness at 0, keeping the mode, and saves it; the second click doesn't also move the thumb.
  It is primary, so the collapsed ribbon keeps it: its icons and track as they are, only as wide as they are, as tall as a small button.
theme: A "Theme" button with a palette icon. Clicking it opens the [ThemeEditorScope](../../theme-editor/index.md#theme-editor-scope). Its tooltip says it chooses the base colour, and the colours of Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask.
  It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon leaves it out.
settings: A "Settings" button with a gear icon. Clicking it opens the [SettingsWindowScope](../../../../scope/settings-window/index.md#settings-window-scope), where the system prompt each chat tab sends is edited. Its tooltip says so, and gives its keyboard shortcut, Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS).
  It is primary, and a full button.
welcome: A "Welcome" button with a checklist icon. Clicking it opens the [WelcomeScope](../../../../scope/welcome/index.md#welcome-scope), running its checks anew. Its tooltip says it checks that Suspense is ready to run.
  It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon leaves it out.
walkthrough: A "Walkthrough" button with a signpost icon. Clicking it starts the [WalkthroughScope](../../../../scope/walkthrough/index.md#walkthrough-scope) from its first step. Its tooltip says it walks through creating a project and the prompt modes.
  It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon leaves it out.
checkForUpdates: A "Check for Updates" button with a refresh icon. Clicking it checks for an update straight away, as the Updates section's Check for updates does, as the [SelfUpdateScope](../../../../scope/self-update/index.md#self-update-scope) says, whether automatic checks are on or not, and says how it went in a notification, which reads "Suspense is up to date", with the version running; "Downloading Suspense 0.1.N…" when a newer release is found, followed by the "Suspense 0.1.N is ready" notification, with its Restart and Later buttons, once it is staged; or, titled "Could not check for updates", why the check or download failed.
  While a check or download is under way, it shows a spinner in place of its icon and is disabled, its tooltip saying what is under way. While an update is already staged, clicking it shows the "Suspense 0.1.N is ready" notification again, without checking. In a build that can't update itself, as one made on a developer's machine, it is disabled, its tooltip saying why, as the Updates section does. Otherwise its tooltip says it checks for a newer version of Suspense.
  It is a full button, and not primary, so the collapsed ribbon leaves it out.
```

It is newer only when its N is greater than the running build's; an older or equal one is never taken, so an update never goes back. A release without the asset for the ru

It says the running version, as "Suspense 0.1.42", and where it can't update itself, as for a build made elsewhere, why, and offers nothing else. Otherwise it shows a checkbox reading "Check for updates automatically", a "Check for updates" button, 
.claude/reference/scope/edge-releases/index.md:15:#### Version
.claude/reference/scope/edge-releases/index.md:17:An edge release's version is `0.1.N`, where N is the commit's sequence number on main: how many commits its history holds, counted by `git rev-list --count` on that commit, so each commit on main has its own number, one more than its parent's, and the same commit always gets the same version. The workflow checks out the whole history to count it, n
.claude/reference/scope/edge-releases/index.md:18:The version is baked into the binary when it is built, so the application knows its own version, and so is the repository it is published from, as `owner/name`, which marks it as an edge build that can update itself. A build made anywhere else, as on a developer's machine, has the version Cargo.toml gives it, and no repository.
.claude/reference/scope/edge-releases/index.md:41:Its assets are one archive per platform, each holding the binary alone, named for the version and the platform:
.claude/reference/scope/edge-releases/index.md:48:If any platform's job fails, nothing is published for that commit, so no edge release ever lacks a platform; the workflow run shows which job failed. A release already published for a version, as when a run is re-run, is never published twice: the run publishes nothing more for it and succeeds.

content.text:
I added an About button to the end of the Application tab's Help group, and an "About Suspense" panel for it to open. `piton check` reports no problems, `piton build` wrote 81 files, and the new page is at `.claude/reference/scope/about/index.md`.

## What changed in the spec

**1. New About panel** (`spec/scope/about/index.pi`)
- **`#description`:** a small panel titled "About Suspense" with a close button. It shows the app icon (64px), "Suspense" in large semibold text, and a muted one-line description.
- **`#details`:** labelled rows, in this order:
  - **Version:** `0.1.N`, followed, muted, by "edge" or "development build".
  - **Commit:** short hash. Left out if the build doesn't record it.
  - **Built:** build date. Left out if the build doesn't record it.
  - **Platform:** for example "Windows x86-64".
  - **Piton:** from `piton --version`, or "Not installed". It reads "Checking…" until that answers, and never delays the panel opening. This is the only command the panel runs.
- **`#links`:** edge builds show a link to the GitHub repository (`owner/name`) and "Release notes" for this version. Development builds show neither.
- **`#actions`:**
  - "Copy details" copies one `Label: value` line per row, starting with "Suspense", for bug reports. It reads "Copied" for 2 seconds after.
  - "Check for Updates", only where the build can update itself.
  - A primary "Close" button, or Escape, closes the panel.

**2. Where it's opened**
- **Ribbon** (`.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/application-tab/index.md`): the Help group now ends Welcome, Walkthrough, Check for Updates, About (`#groups`). The new "About" button (`#commands`) has an info icon and is a full button that the collapsed ribbon leaves out, like its neighbours.
- **Main window** (`.claude/reference/scope/application/MainWindow.md#about`): it opens in the inset panel, replacing whatever is there, as Settings does.
- **Palette:** a new "About Suspense" command opens it.

**For the code step:** the commit and build-date rows assume the build records them, but the spec doesn't yet say it does. The code needs to bake them into the binary when it is built, as it already does the version; until then those rows are simply left out.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791134167-AddAboutButton.understanding.md`.

## Anchors the code should follow
- `AboutScope`: `#description`, `#details`, `#links`, `#actions`.
- `RibbonApplicationTabScope`: `#groups`, `#commands` (`about`).
- `MainWindowScope`: `#about`.
- `PaletteScope`: its system commands.
- `EdgeReleasesScope`: `#version`, for the baked-in version and repository.
- `SelfUpdateScope`: for the panel's Check for Updates button.
